phase: W2b-4a: the browser host's saves kept in the browser
change: web_run.mjs --persist GUEST (with --canvas): a mount the page keeps in the browser's IndexedDB ('ntsd-save', one record per entry keyed by its guest path, {dir, data}); the runner never serves it. The worker never yields while the game runs, so the page loads the mount's whole tree before the worker starts (both the scripted and interactive paths) and the worker sends each change back as a message (a closed or synced file's bytes, a folder made, an unlink, an rmdir, a rename); the page stores them in order, each in a readwrite transaction with strict durability, a file replaced whole, a rename replacing its target and moving a folder's subtree. At exit the worker counts its store messages into the frame header; the page stores all of them (within the worker's 5 s) before it acknowledges, and with --metrics reports what the browser keeps (path, size, SHA-256). Failures are shown to the player (a notice) and reported on stderr; a connection the browser closed is opened again; a page without IndexedDB plays without saving; a second tab of the game plays without saving (a Web Lock held for the page's life); navigator.storage.persist() is asked. --profile DIR keeps a browser profile between runs and --port PORT keeps one origin (the browser keeps storage per origin, port included); localhost is redirected to 127.0.0.1 for the same reason. The worker's rename now answers as rename(2) (the same entry, into itself, file onto folder, folder onto file or a non-empty folder); a kept file's bytes stay after close. No Swift change: the host already wrote its overlay to /save/NTSD Native when the page mounts /save.

review: Round 1 (independent, read-only): high (latent): fd_close released an unchanged file's bytes, which a kept mount cannot read back, so a second open of a save in one session would read it empty; medium: an interactive start with IndexedDB unavailable would hang on a black page; medium: a connection the browser closed (iOS Safari) would fail every later save silently, failures went only to stderr; low: the key range's upper bound, rename into its own subtree and rename(2)'s checks, seed conflicts, --port/EADDRINUSE handling, localhost vs 127.0.0.1 as two origins, finish's waits vs the worker's 5 s and hashing, two tabs racing, eviction. Fixed: all but the seed conflict's orphans and lazy loading (documented boundaries). Round 2: medium: the fallback without saving (a second tab, no IndexedDB) removed the mount, shifting the worker's mount numbering, and the host's temporary overlay is not mounted in the browser; fixed by keeping the mount in place (loaded read-only or empty, its changes not stored, the player told); low: one retry for any error but a full quota, the lock released when loading fails, a synchronous open failure; fixed. Round 3: OK; one low item left (opened() keeps a rejected promise when indexedDB.open throws synchronously, since ??= assigns after the executor; harmless now, queued for W2b-4b). The files tested: run.html, wasi-worker.js, web_run.mjs, web_saves_check.py unchanged from before the saves check to after the regression (SHA-256 checked).
boundaries: A change still being stored when the tab closes is lost (milliseconds after the game wrote it)
Every kept file is loaded into the page and the worker at each start (recordings included)
The browser may evict the storage: persist() is asked; Safari caps a site's script-writable storage at 7 days without a visit unless the page is a home-screen app
A second tab plays without saving
A record whose path runs through a stored file (a conflict) is ignored at load and stays stored
Safari and Firefox are not tried; WebKit is Playwright's build
